description: "The moment the SQL Server engine stops accepting Kerberos tickets and Windows challenge-response and starts accepting Entra ID-issued OAuth 2.0 tokens. ::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
# Book_05 — The Login Migration: Windows Principals to Entra Logins
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Everything in Books 01 through 04 is prerequisite; everything in Books 06 through 09 is consequence. This book is the migration itself — performed only on the instances Book 02 classified **retain** or **target**, using the three-phase parallel-run pattern that ADR-091 makes normative. (ADR-091)
:::

![During: two client types simultaneously active — legacy Kerberos/NTLM and migrated Entra token — sharing one SQL Server.](images/card-during-01-overview.svg){#fig-book-05-card-during-01 fig-alt="Card diagram on white background. Title: DURING — Two Paths, One Destination (1 of 3: Overview). Two client boxes: Client A Not Yet Migrated in red, Client B Migrated in teal. Center: Domain Controller (dashed red) and Entra ID (teal). Right: SQL Server with type-W, type-E, and type-S login badges. Footer explains the hybrid state is a controlled risk. Navy, teal, red palette." width="100%"}

![During: the three-phase parallel-run pattern — Add the Entra login, validate it against real traffic for 30 days, then retire the Windows login.](images/card-during-02-parallelrun.svg){#fig-book-05-card-during-02 fig-alt="Card diagram on white background. Title: DURING — Two Paths, One Destination (2 of 3: The Parallel-Run Pattern). Three phase columns with vertical dashed dividers. Two login track rows: Windows login in red, Entra login in teal. Three detail boxes below: what you do, what you verify, what you remove. Footer: ADR-091 makes this three-phase pattern normative." width="100%"}

![During: the three costs every unmigrated login carries — CA blind spot, NTLM exposure, and the hard 2027-04-01 deadline.](images/card-during-03-risk.svg){#fig-book-05-card-during-03 fig-alt="Card diagram on white background. Title: DURING — Two Paths, One Destination (3 of 3: What Every Unmigrated Login Costs). Three red risk cards: Conditional Access blind spot, NTLM Exposure still present, Hard Deadline approaching. Navy footer: the hybrid window is not a neutral holding pattern." width="100%"}

![During the login migration, both authentication paths reach the same SQL Server. Legacy connections use Kerberos or NTLM through the domain controller; migrated connections present an Entra token. The parallel-run window keeps both active until every legacy login is validated, disabled, observed for 30 days, and dropped.](images/wan-02-hybrid-migration-state.svg){#fig-book-05-wan-02 fig-alt="WAN topology diagram showing the hybrid migration state with two client types, Entra ID for the new path, the domain controller for the old path, and SQL Server accepting both type-W and type-E logins simultaneously. Progress bars at the bottom show the estate at 40% login migration completion. Navy, teal, red, amber palette, white background." width="100%"}

![Simplified migration state: two client types, two authentication paths, one SQL Server. The hybrid window stays open until every legacy login is migrated.](images/wan-simple-02-migration.svg){#fig-book-05-wan-simple-02 fig-alt="Simplified WAN diagram showing two client boxes — Not Yet Migrated in red and Migrated in teal — feeding two separate paths to SQL Server. The old path routes through the Domain Controller using Kerberos or NTLM. The new path goes directly to Entra ID and arrives at SQL Server as an OAuth 2.0 token. Bottom bar explains that the hybrid state is a controlled risk, not a stable destination, and closes at 2027-04-01. White background, navy, teal, red, amber palette." width="100%"}

![The parallel run, then the switch: the old Windows login and the new Entra login carry the same principal side by side until the legacy track is retired.](images/book05-image-01-parallel-run.png){#fig-book-05-image-01 fig-alt="An illustrative figure on a white background showing two parallel tracks across three phases — 'Phase 1, add', 'Phase 2, run in parallel', 'Phase 3, cut over'. A stylised principal silhouette on the left ('user, group, service') feeds two arrows: a grey arrow up to a 'Windows login (Kerberos ticket / NTLM)' box and a teal arrow down to an 'Entra login (FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER)' box. The Windows-login track continues as a grey dashed line labelled 'still works — kept as the rollback path' and ends at a red crossed-out circle labelled 'old login removed'. The Entra-login track continues as a solid teal arrow labelled 'validated in parallel against real traffic' into a navy 'SQL Server engine' box reading 'accepts Entra-issued OAuth tokens'. Illustrative register (ADR-095): navy (#0D1B2E), teal (#1E8C8C) for the new path, grey for the legacy path, red (#C0392B) for removal; stylised silhouette, no photographs; 16:9 landscape. A footer line notes the figure is illustrative — the phases are conceptual, not a schedule or measured cutover." width="100%"}
